341752.title: Marton's Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture over finite fields
341752.statement: Let $p$ be a prime, let $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^n$ satisfy $|A+A|\leqslant K|A|$, and let $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^N$ be a set. Equivalently, let $\phi:\mathbb{F}_p^n\to\mathbb{F}_p^N$ be a function such that $\phi(x+y)-\phi(x)-\phi(y)$ takes values in $S$. **Marton's Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture.** There is a linear map $\tilde{\phi}:\mathbb{F}_p^n\to\mathbb{F}_p^N$ such that $\phi-\tilde{\phi}$ takes at most $|S|^{O(1)}$ values; equivalently, $A$ can be covered by at most $K^{O(1)}$ translates of a subspace of size at most $K^{O(1)}|A|$. This is a central structural conjecture in additive combinatorics; the paper uses its equivalent formulation to motivate a stronger variant, which it then discusses via a counterexample.

341753.title: Strong Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture for approximate homomorphisms
341753.statement: Let $p$ be a prime, and let $\phi:\mathbb{F}_p^n\to\mathbb{F}_p^N$ be a function such that $\phi(x+y)-\phi(x)-\phi(y)$ takes values in a set $S$. Let $K$ be the doubling parameter from the equivalent additive-combinatorial formulation $|A+A|\leqslant K|A|$. **Strong Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture.** There is a linear map $\tilde{\phi}:\mathbb{F}_p^n\to\mathbb{F}_p^N$ such that $\phi-\tilde{\phi}$ takes values in $tS$, for some constant $t$ depending only on $K$. The paper states this as a strong variant of the Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture and discusses a counterexample to it, so the variant is refuted.

342072.title: The conjecture that the union of two arithmetic progressions is not sum-dominant
342072.statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be arithmetic progressions of integers, and consider their union $A\cup B$. A finite set $S$ of integers is **sum-dominant** if $|S+S|>|S-S|$, where $S+S=\{s_1+s_2:s_1,s_2\in S\}$ and $S-S=\{s_1-s_2:s_1,s_2\in S\}$. **Non-sum-dominance conjecture.** The union $A\cup B$ is not a sum-dominant set, that is, $|A\cup B+A\cup B|\leq |A\cup B-A\cup B|$. This is posed as a future research question; no proof or counterexample is supplied in the source.

343949.title: The stronger bipartite rainbow matching conjecture
343949.statement:
Let $f_{\mathcal B}(n,m)$ be the least number of $n$-element matchings in a bipartite graph that guarantees a rainbow matching of size $m$. **Strong bipartite rainbow matching conjecture.**

$$
f_{\mathcal B}(n,n-1)=n-1.
$$

Equivalently, every $n-1$ matchings of size $n$ in a bipartite graph have a full rainbow matching. The source explicitly states that this is false for general graphs, giving a counterexample construction.

343968.title: Duality conjecture for ideal access structures
343968.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an access structure. It is **ideal** if it can be realized by an ideal entropic polymatroid, equivalently by an ideal distribution scheme. Let $\mathcal A^\bot$ denote the dual access structure. **Duality conjecture for ideal structures.** The dual of an ideal access structure is ideal.

This is a particular case of the broader conjecture that entropic complexity is invariant under duality. The source says that this special case had resisted all efforts and that refuting it does not necessarily refute the broader conjecture, since the dual might be non-ideal while having complexity $1$. The parser marks this conjecture as disproved.

344911.title: Global persistence conjecture for simple eigenvector solutions
344911.statement: Let $(x_*,0,\lambda_*)$ be a simple solution of the eigenvalue problem, meaning that the first three hypotheses stated in the paper hold. Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are separable, and that $N$ and $C$ are compact. **Global persistence conjecture.** The set of nontrivial solutions has a connected subset whose closure contains $(x_*,0,\lambda_*)$ and is either unbounded or meets a trivial solution $(x^*,0,\lambda^*)$ with $\lambda^*\ne\lambda_*$. The conjecture would sharpen the preceding global continuation theorem from eigenpairs to eigenvector solutions in the infinite-dimensional setting; the authors state that they have not been able either to prove or to disprove it.

345244.title: The conditions (S1) and (S2) imply hypergroup structure
345244.statement: Let $(\Gamma,w_0)$ be a pointed graph satisfying the conditions $(S1)$ and $(S2)$. Say that it **produces a hypergroup** when its associated distance distribution yields a hypergroup. **Hypergroup conjecture.** The conditions $(S1)$ and $(S2)$ imply that $(\Gamma,w_0)$ produces a hypergroup. The authors report that all known examples satisfying these conditions produce hypergroups, but no general proof or counterexample is given.

346674.title: Breit–Wigner divergence alternative under Froese's hypotheses
346674.statement:
Let $V$ be a super-exponentially decreasing potential, let $\widehat V$ have completely regular growth, and let $B(V)$ be its Breit–Wigner series. Assume that $V$ is not compactly supported. **Breit–Wigner divergence alternative.** Either $B(V)$ diverges, or $V$ is a counterexample to Froese's conjecture.

This is presented as a weaker form of the paper's stronger Breit–Wigner convergence conjecture. It links divergence of the resonance series for noncompactly supported potentials to the possible failure of Froese's resonance-counting estimate.

350410.title: Harrington–Henninger-Voss–Karhadkar–Robinson–Wong sum–difference index inequality conjecture
350410.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, with sum index $\operatorname{sum}(G)$ and difference index $\operatorname{dif}(G)$ defined using injective integer vertex labellings and, respectively, the edge labels $f(u)+f(v)$ and $|f(u)-f(v)|$. **Harrington–Henninger-Voss–Karhadkar–Robinson–Wong's conjecture.** Every nonempty simple graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\left\lceil \operatorname{sum}(G)/2\right\rceil\leq\operatorname{dif}(G)\leq\operatorname{sum}(G).
$$

This was proposed as a modification after counterexamples to the preceding equality conjecture. The paper states that its results still disprove this modified conjecture in a strong sense.

351476.title: Non-Sidorenko conjecture for $(2 \times 5)$-systems
351476.statement: Let $L$ be a $(2\times 5)$-system of linear equations, and let $s(L)$ denote the parameter used in the paper. Assume that $s(L)=4$. **Non-Sidorenko conjecture.** Every $(2\times 5)$-system with $s(L)=4$ is not Sidorenko. This conjecture arises from the paper's progress toward characterising Sidorenko $(2\times k)$-systems. Apart from the cases established in the paper and the referenced counterexample, the relevant cases remain open.

352298.title: Separation conjecture for adjacent spine vertices
352298.statement: Let $G$ be an augmented caterpillar drawn as a great-circle thrackle, and let $v$ and $v'$ be adjacent vertices in the spine of $G$. A **separating $2$-path at a vertex** is a $2$-path that separates at that vertex. **Separation conjecture for adjacent spine vertices.** If some $2$-path separates at $v$, then no $2$-path separates at $v'$. The conjecture further specifies the possible structure of great-circle thrackleable augmented caterpillars; the source leaves it open and suggests that crossing orientations could help prove or refute it.

352675.title: The comb-domain generic-position conjecture for KdV frequencies
352675.statement: Let $\eta=\{\eta_k\}_{k\geq1}$ and $\eta^{(1)}=\{\eta_k^{(1)}\}_{k\geq1}$ be the frequency collections associated with the comb domains describing the KdV flows. **Comb-domain generic-position conjecture.** With a fixed collection $\eta$, one can bring $\eta^{(1)}$ into a generic position by an arbitrarily small variation of $\{h_k\}_{k\geq1}$. This is a proposed step in the paper's program for constructing a counterexample; the supplied text gives no resolution.

353070.title: The quadratic spectral containment conjecture for multiaffine stable polynomials
353070.statement: A homogeneous multiaffine stable polynomial is a stable polynomial that is homogeneous and multiaffine. **Quadratic spectral containment conjecture.** Every quadratic homogeneous multiaffine stable polynomial has the spectral containment property. This is highlighted as a potentially tractable special case because quadratic multiaffine polynomials have especially simple minor lifts; no proof or counterexample is given.

353123.title: The cyclic matroid wheel, whirl, spike and swirl conjecture
353123.statement:
Let $s$ be an integer exceeding two, and let $M$ be an $(s,s)$-cyclic matroid.

**Cyclic matroid structure conjecture.** If $s$ is even, then $M$ can be obtained from a spike or a swirl by a sequence of inflations. If $s$ is odd, then $M$ can be obtained from a wheel or a whirl by a sequence of inflations.

This conjecture was posed in the study of matroids with prescribed circuits and cocircuits. The paper gives a counterexample to it, so the asserted classification by inflations is false.

353422.title: Defective Goldberg-Seymour conjecture
353422.statement:
Let $d\in\mathbb N^*$ and let $G$ be a graph. Define

$$
\Gamma_d(G)=\max\left\{\left\lceil \frac{|E(G[X])|}{\left\lfloor d|X|/2\right\rfloor}\right\rceil\mathrel{:}X\subseteq V(G)\right\}.
$$

**Defective Goldberg-Seymour conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi'_d(G)\leq \max\left\{\Gamma_d(G),\left\lceil \frac{\Delta(G)+1}{d}\right\rceil\right\}.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of the Goldberg-Seymour bound to defective edge colouring; no proof or counterexample is supplied in the source.

353625.title: The retract-image conjecture for non-bipartite generalized Petersen graphs
353625.statement:
Let $G(n,k)$ be a non-bipartite generalized Petersen graph, and let $f$ be an endomorphism of $G(n,k)$. The **retract-image conjecture.** The image of $f$ is a retract of $G(n,k)$.

The claim concerns the structure of endomorphism images. The source notes that it fails for bipartite generalized Petersen graphs, giving the Möbius–Kantor graph $G(8,3)$ as a counterexample, but gives no resolution for the non-bipartite case.

353943.title: The graphicness conjecture for 3-connected orderable binary matroids
353943.statement: A **matroid** $M$ is **orderable** if it admits an ordering of its circuits with the relevant ordering property, and it is **3-connected** and **binary** in the usual matroid-theoretic senses. **Graphicness conjecture.** A $3$-connected orderable binary matroid is graphic. Although there are orderable binary matroids that are not graphic, no counterexample is known; the conjecture would distinguish graphic matroids within the class of binary matroids.

354292.title: Frankl's product conjecture for rainbow-triangle-free graph triples
354292.statement:
Let $G_1,G_2,G_3$ be graphs with a common vertex set on $n$ vertices. A **rainbow triangle** is a triangle whose three edges belong to three distinct graphs among $G_1,G_2,G_3$. **Frankl's conjecture.** If the graphs have no rainbow triangle, then

$$
e(G_1)e(G_2)e(G_3)\leq \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor^3.
$$

The bound is attained by taking three copies of a complete bipartite graph with parts as equal as possible. Frankl proved the conjecture under the additional assumptions $E(G_1)\subseteq E(G_2)$ and $E(G_1)\subseteq E(G_3)$, but the paper gives a counterexample in general, so the conjecture is false.

354889.title: Aharoni–Korman fish bone conjecture for bounded-width posets
354889.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset of bounded width: there is a finite number $k$ such that every antichain $A$ satisfies $|A|\leq k$. A **chain** is a totally ordered subset of $P$, and a decomposition of $V(P)$ into disjoint antichains is a partition of the elements of $P$ into antichains.

**Fish bone conjecture.** There exist a chain $C$ and a decomposition $D$ of $V(P)$ into disjoint antichains such that every antichain in $D$ meets $C$.

This conjecture is trivial for finite posets and follows from the edge-cover version of the preceding hypergraph conjecture together with compactness. It is known for $k=2$, but remains open in general; the source notes that even the case with no infinite antichains has no known counterexample.

355966.title: Linear-type conjecture for trees and unicyclic graphs
355966.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $J_G$ be its binomial edge ideal, and say that $J_G$ is **of linear type** when its Rees algebra is generated by the degree-one part in the standard sense. **Linear-type conjecture for trees and unicyclic graphs.** If $G$ is a tree or a unicyclic graph, then

$$
J_G\text{ is of linear type}.
$$

The source presents this as a statement to prove or disprove after noting that the preceding classification question is not true for trees; it gives no resolution.
